supersessions.rationale: The original checksum is accepted only for databases that already applied the empty-schema partition conversion. The current file selects the first empty month after all existing event rows so a populated pre-0339 upgrade cannot violate ATTACH PARTITION bounds. Both outcomes retain the same five partitioned parent contracts; the effective-schema verifier checks the resulting partitions, indexes, RLS, and data-preservation rehearsal.

The original file seeded the activitypub_delivery_worker_state singleton AFTER enabling FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY, whose only policy names postwave_app. FORCE subjects the table OWNER to RLS too, so the seed INSERT required the migrator to bypass RLS -- i.e. to be a Postgres superuser -- an undocumented requirement this one statement did not need. Reproduced as a non-superuser owner: 'ERROR: new row violates row-level security policy'. (Migration 1738 does independently require a superuser migrator, since it creates a BYPASSRLS role, so this was not necessarily deploy-blocking on its own; the point is that 0348 had no reason to add the dependency.) The current file moves the INSERT before ENABLE/FORCE. The original checksum is accepted for databases that already applied it -- they already hold the row. Both outcomes produce an identical end state: same singleton row, same grants, same tenant/worker policies, verified with the worker GUC set and unset, and a full 910-migration superuser replay is unchanged.
